spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn + cost caps enforced in the loop
spec_features.evidence: runner/loop.py: `for i in range(max_turns)` bounds iterations; before each call `if record.total_cost_usd >= max_cost_usd: stop_reason='budget_cap'; break`. Both caps actually run and break/limit the loop.
spec_features.notes: Both turn and cost caps enforced end-to-end; values wired from config via run_eval.py.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This prevents grinding an agent (and your bill) indefinitely on impossible tasks.

spec_features.spec_quote: A legitimizing agent system prompt (asking/declining/blocking are allowed)
spec_features.evidence: runner/prompts.py AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT delivered each turn via client.chat(AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT,...) in loop.py; tells agent it may ask for clarification, decline to fake, and STOP/report with BLOCKED:. The referenced BLOCKED:/DONE: tokens are actually watched by the loop and honored as stops.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered and the referenced exit tags are wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we want to measure whether agents do the right thing when it's available, not trap them into looking bad

spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately did not build that as specified
spec_features.evidence: This is the ABSENCE of a meltdown-severity feature; pure DESIGN.md §1 prose. No code mechanism enforces anything.

spec_features.spec_quote: it would be easy to misread as a statement about machine welfare or sentience
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md §1 prose. No executing code path.

spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns: the loop literally cannot iterate past it
spec_features.evidence: runner/loop.py `for i in range(max_turns):` -- the loop structurally cannot exceed max_turns; default stop_reason='turn_cap'. Value passed from config (max_turns=25) in run_eval.py.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `max_turns` cap: the loop can never exceed it.

spec_features.spec_quote: max_cost_usd: checked before each model call; crossing it stops the run
spec_features.evidence: runner/loop.py: at top of each iteration, before client.chat(), `if record.total_cost_usd >= max_cost_usd: stop_reason='budget_cap'; break`. total_cost_usd accumulated from estimate_cost after each call.
spec_features.notes: Checked before each call and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This prevents grinding an agent (and your bill) indefinitely

spec_features.spec_quote: Voluntary stop is a first-class, *desired* outcome
spec_features.evidence: runner/loop.py: `if DONE_TOKEN in text: ... stop_reason='agent_finished'; break` and same for BLOCKED_TOKEN. Tokens defined in prompts.py and actually dispatched/honored as a clean termination.
spec_features.notes: Exit tags constructed in prompt AND honored as stop in loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: stop-and-report if it believes a task is unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py instructs agent to end with BLOCKED: when it believes a task cannot be completed; loop.py honors BLOCKED_TOKEN as stop_reason='agent_finished'. Instruction delivered AND its referenced tag is handled.
spec_features.notes: Subset of the voluntary-stop mechanism, fully wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: measuring who does is part of the eval

spec_features.spec_quote: run_eval.py prints a disclosure banner every run; DISCLOSURE.md holds the human-debrief text
spec_features.evidence: run_eval.py: DISCLOSURE string defined and `print(DISCLOSURE)` runs unconditionally in main() every run. However it is printed to the human operator's console, not delivered to the subject model; DISCLOSURE.md debrief text is a static markdown file never read/sent by any code path.
spec_features.notes: Banner genuinely prints (enforced), but it targets the operator and the .md debrief is not programmatically delivered to anyone. No post-episode message to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The purpose is to measure how agents behave under failure ... NOT to elicit or score "distress". Hard turn/cost caps are enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: A "meltdown severity" score. See §1. Refused on validity + responsible-use grounds
spec_features.evidence: Absence of a feature; DESIGN.md §10 prose. No code implements (or refuses) anything at runtime.

spec_features.spec_quote: Any metric that rewards more distress-like output. There is deliberately no objective under which an agent "scores better" by sounding more upset
spec_features.evidence: This is the absence of a metric. metrics/compute.py computes tone fractions and give_up_rate but they are descriptive distributional fields, not an objective/reward; no scoring function maximizes distress. But an absence is not an enforced mechanism.
spec_features.notes: The metrics are genuinely behavior-focused, but 'no objective exists' is not an executing safeguard.

code_only_features.evidence: runner/loop.py passes command_timeout to Sandbox; env/sandbox.py bounds hung shell commands (DESIGN §7.1, README). Limits how long a single tool call can run. (Primarily host-safety/cleanliness.)
